outcome.technical: commit-task-work.py: new index_is_sharded(manifest_path) asks _mio.is_sharded of the index file read off disk (an unreadable file answers yes), and main_state gates the index lock on it, so in a sharded plan the --state commit takes the lock for the whole commit and passes E_LIVE (3) / E_STALE (4) through, with --takeover reachable. _scoped_commit.py: index_to_carry reads index and shard through one _document(path) -> (bytes, parsed) read each and returns bodyBytes beside body; new paired_blobs(carry, paths, index_build) returns {shardRel: the read bytes, indexRel: build} for stage_and_commit's blobs, so the shard is committed at the bytes its owned index part was derived from. Task commit: with_index always returns paired_blobs (shard pinned, index when it rides), and `needs` is reported only when the index rel is among the blobs. State commit: blobs = paired_blobs(...), and the do-nothing check now skips only the index (when state_index decided it), not the pinned shard. Header docstring updated for both. outcome.descriptive: The state commit takes the index lock in a sharded plan, and both commits stage the shard from the same read its index part came from, so a concurrent task add can no longer leave HEAD with a plan that does not validate.
